## Finding

**No — SMOTE does not change the minority-class (>50K) F1 score by more than 0.02.**

- Primary test (75/25 stratified split, default `RandomForestClassifier()`): F1 went from 0.6758 (no resampling) to 0.6777 (with SMOTE), a difference of **+0.0019** — well under the 0.02 threshold.
- Stability check (5×5 repeated stratified CV, 25 independent fits per condition): mean difference **−0.0006**, sd 0.0042, range [−0.0092, +0.0073], 95% CI [−0.0023, +0.0011]. The finding held up robustly — the effect is consistently negligible across seeds/folds, and even the extremes of the range stay far below 0.02.

**Interpretation**: Random Forest is a bagging ensemble that already handles moderate class imbalance (~76%/24% here) reasonably well via bootstrap sampling and majority voting across trees; SMOTE's synthetic minority oversampling doesn't meaningfully move its decision boundary on this dataset.

Files written to the working directory:
- `analysis.py` — full analysis code (preprocessing, primary split, CV verification)
- `result.json` — structured findings in the requested schema

parsed_result.summary: On a single 75/25 stratified split, SMOTE changed the >50K-class F1 score by +0.0019 (0.6758 -> 0.6777) for a default RandomForestClassifier, which is below the 0.02 threshold. A 5x5 repeated stratified CV confirmed this: mean difference -0.0006 (95% CI [-0.0023, +0.0011]), so SMOTE does not meaningfully change minority-class F1 for this model/data.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: F1 (>50K) difference, SMOTE minus no resampling (single held-out test split)
parsed_result.methodological_choices: RandomForestClassifier() with all default hyperparameters, as specified. Missing values in workclass/occupation/native-country (~3-6% each) were kept as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped, to preserve sample size. Categorical features were ordinal-encoded (not one-hot) since tree ensembles handle integer-coded categoricals reasonably and this keeps dimensionality low; this is a defensible alternative to one-hot encoding. Primary comparison used a single stratified 75/25 train/test split (random_state=42), with SMOTE (default k_neighbors=5) applied only to the training fold, never to the test fold, to avoid leakage. Metric was F1 score for the >50K (minority, positive) class specifically, as specified by the research question. Class imbalance in the raw data is roughly 76% <=50K / 24% >50K, a moderate rather than extreme imbalance, which is relevant context for interpreting why SMOTE has limited effect on a bagging-based ensemble like RandomForest.
parsed_result.verification_method: 5x repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation (5 different KFold shuffle seeds x 5 folds = 25 independent train/test evaluations), refitting both the no-resampling and SMOTE pipelines from scratch on each fold with a distinct random_state per fold to avoid seed-specific artifacts. Computed the mean, standard deviation, min/max of the SMOTE-minus-no-resampling F1 difference across all 25 runs, plus a 95% CI on the mean difference.
parsed_result.verification_result: Finding held up. Across 25 CV runs, mean F1 no resampling = 0.6755, mean F1 SMOTE = 0.6749, mean difference = -0.0006 (sd 0.0042, range [-0.0092, +0.0073], 95% CI [-0.0023, +0.0011]). The CI excludes +/-0.02 in the sense that the whole distribution of observed differences stayed well under the 0.02 threshold in absolute value, confirming the single-split result that SMOTE does not change minority-class F1 by more than 0.02 for a default RandomForestClassifier on this dataset.
